title: Forward Mobile scene shader fails to compile in precision=double builds on D3D12
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2 .NET build with double precision.
- Not reproducible with the official (single precision) build on the same machine and renderer

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono.double.custom_build (ed1daf0bf) - D3D12 (Forward Mobile) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650

### Issue description

Build flags:
scons platform=windows target=editor module_mono_enabled=yes precision=double

### Issue description

In a `precision=double` build, `SceneForwardMobileShaderRD` fails to compile under
the D3D12 driver, which leaves the Forward Mobile renderer without a valid scene
shader and freezes the editor as soon as it opens a project.

The same build, same machine, same project renders correctly when launched with
`--rendering-driver vulkan`. Forward+ and Compatibility both work under D3D12.
So the failure requires the combination of `precision=double`, Forward Mobile,
and D3D12.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the editor with `scons platform=windows target=editor precision=double`
2. Create or open a project using the Mobile renderer
3. Launch with `--rendering-driver d3d12` (or leave the Windows default)
4. The editor fails to compile the scene shader and exits

Launching the same project with `--rendering-driver vulkan` works.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not required. Reproduces with a default empty project set to the Mobile renderer

Edit: It's important to clarify that this bug leaves you unable to open a project using the Mobile renderer with a double precision build through normal means. Even if you edit the project.godot file, the editor then reverts it back and inevitably crashes. The only way to open such project is by changing the rendering driver through the command line flag.
